body.x: Rovigos (CEO Kim Tae-yong) participated in CES 2024 in Las Vegas from January 9th to 12th.

As an artificial intelligence cloud specialist startup, Rovigos analyzes corporate data and provides data analysis and optimal AI solutions according to customer requests. The solutions address inconveniences arising in various aspects of logistics.

One of the solutions, the TMS (Transportation Management System), utilizes Rovigos AI to reduce management, transportation, and loading costs and derive the most efficient transportation methods in the distribution process. The company explains that it optimizes the distribution process, resolving logistical challenges for logistics companies.

Additionally, Rovigos aims to lead the future logistics industry using UAM (Urban Air Mobility)/drone technology. The company has participated in Korea’s UAM introduction process, the ‘K-UAM Grand Challenge.’ It has the goal of advancing existing control technologies to realize UAM/drone delivery in the future.

Furthermore, Rovigos addresses issues during long-distance maritime transportation through its innovative container solution. Maintaining a consistent temperature is crucial for preserving the value of products such as fresh food or pharmaceuticals during naval transportation. Combining AI and IoT technologies, the solution enables remote control and monitoring.

Regarding this solution, a Rovigos representative mentioned, “We learned that a significant economic loss occurs in the maritime transportation industry due to the disposal of a large amount of food and pharmaceuticals every year. This loss is mainly confirmed due to the failure of temperature and humidity control inside the containers.” The representative explained, “We thought such issues could be resolved if there was a product with real-time monitoring and remote control capabilities. Thus, we created ‘Fresh Guard’ and designed it with a digital twin, communication IoT, and other features to optimize the process.”
The strengths of ‘Fresh Guard’ include remote control of temperature and humidity. It optimizes the container environment remotely, ensuring product quality maintenance and reducing losses.

Moreover, using digital twin technology, the product virtually represents the inside of shipping containers in virtual reality, preventing theft, robbery, and loss. The solution utilizes IoT-equipped satellite modules to monitor the real-time status and conditions of DB-sized containers hourly.

Rovigos, recognized for its technological capabilities, was selected as a ‘Chogokcha Startup’ (Superior Startup) in early August and has also been chosen for collaborative R&D through ‘Chogokcha Startup’ linkage. In October, the company was selected for cooperation with Shinhan Square Bridge (OurHome) and won the Ulsan Port Authority President’s Award.

A representative stated, “Through participation in CES 2024, we aim to introduce our groundbreaking products and solutions to a global audience, receive feedback, and measure market interest. This will contribute to improving our products and customizing them to meet specific demands and preferences of target customers.” The representative added, “We plan to leverage the momentum gained at CES to secure strategic partnerships and collaborations. Additionally, we aim to strengthen research and development initiatives to stay at the forefront of technological innovation within the industry.”
